name: CNH Industrial N.V.
moat_justification: Number-two global ag-equipment franchise (Case IH + New Holland, ~12-14% global share vs Deere's ~18-20%) with a real dealer network, captive finance arm and a parts/service installed base — but returns prove it is narrow, not wide: ROE fell from 28.1% (FY2023) to 16.2% (FY2024) to 6.6% (FY2025), i.e. at/below cost of capital at the trough, and gross margin (31.5-32.7% on total revenues incl. Financial Services) is defended by mix, not pricing power — Agriculture net sales fell 11.5% in FY2025 with North America down 26.4%. Deere's integrated precision ecosystem is stronger; Raven gives CNH a credible but not leading tech stack.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.8%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, accession 0001567094-26-000006), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: 'Expenditures for property, plant and equipment and intangible assets, excluding assets under operating leases' $543M (2025) / $536M (2024) / $644M (2023) plus 'Expenditures for assets under operating leases' $655M / $650M / $551M — totals $1,198M / $1,186M / $1,195M); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 1.04 vs 3-yr median 0.56 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
one_liner: Cyclical No.2 ag/construction equipment maker with a captive finance arm, moat 4/10 — at $11.60 it clears nothing: weighted IRR 5.3% on the TTM trough base (IV@15% $2.76), Tier D in every scenario; it would need to trade near $2.76 to clear a 15% hurdle on trough owner's earnings.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: #2 global ag equipment share (~12-14%) via Case IH and New Holland dual brands
Global dealer network plus captive Financial Services ($23.1B financing receivables) that finances a large share of its own sales
Installed-base parts and service annuity across a long-lived fleet
Raven precision-ag technology stack and full-line breadth (ag + construction)
moat_against: Deere's stronger precision ecosystem, brand and pricing power; AGCO/Kubota pressure from both ends
Pure cyclicality: farm-income-driven volumes, FY2025 Agriculture sales -11.5% (North America -26.4%), ROE 28.1% -> 6.6% in two years
Tariff exposure and South America weakness compressed Agriculture adjusted EBIT margin to 5.2% in Q2 2026
Thin equity under a large captive-finance balance sheet; consolidated net debt $23.4B (mostly FS, but the risk is CNH's)

overrides.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26, accession 0001567094-26-000006), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: 'Expenditures for property, plant and equipment and intangible assets, excluding assets under operating leases' $543M (2025) / $536M (2024) / $644M (2023) plus 'Expenditures for assets under operating leases' $655M / $650M / $551M — totals $1,198M / $1,186M / $1,195M
